name: HOLLYWOOD & VINYL
notes: Verified the Saturday Night Fever soundtrack's 24 straight weeks at No. 1 and O Brother's 2002 Album of the Year; no lyrics quoted.

name: ANTHEMOLOGY
notes: France to Cyprus all accurate; Wilhelmus acrostic and the shared Greek-Cypriot anthem check out, titles only, no lyric quoting.

name: SEA TO SHINING C
notes: Bates, Guthrie, Howe, the 1987 National March act and the Johnson brothers all verified; top two rows sit a shade easy for their values.

name: GREAT HALLS OF FIRE
notes: Confirmed Ryman was built by a riverboat captain as an 1892 gospel tabernacle; Carnegie, Apollo, CBGB, Bayreuth all correct.

name: MUD, SWEAT & CHEERS
notes: Yasgur's farm to the Proms; Altamont stabbing and Henry Wood's 1895 first Promenade concert both accurate.

name: FRETS ABOUT NOTHING
notes: Banjo to bouzouki all accurate and well hedged ('often read as' for ukulele); the fretless oud sits oddly under a fret pun.

name: KEYBOARD WARRIORS
notes: Verified Tchaikovsky's secret Mustel celesta order from Paris; accordion patent, Moog, Hammond's clock-making past and Cristofori all correct.

name: TREBLE WITH THE LAW
notes: Checked the 1985 RIAA settlement label wording, which did read Parental Advisory; payola, Louie Louie, Harrisongs and Campbell v. Acuff-Rose all accurate.

name: AGITPOP
notes: Seeger's role properly hedged as 'helped turn'; Meeropol, Simone and the Grandola broadcast all correct, and only titles are quoted.

name: TRACKED HOUSING
notes: Sun to Hansa; Electric Lady's 1970 opening weeks before Hendrix's death and Bowie's 'Hall by the Wall' nickname both verified.

name: PRODUCER'S SURPLUS
notes: Verified Wexler coined 'rhythm and blues' at Billboard; $400 says Quincy Jones 'arranged' Thriller, true but understating his producer credit.

name: JARGON BELLS
notes: Encore to tritone all accurate; syncopation at $1200 is arguably easier than leitmotif at $800, a mild wobble in an otherwise clean ramp.
